value: oriented towards vertical bars occupying 50 deg of the arena wall and above
method: orientation of freely moving animals placed at the centre of a circular arena (60 cm diameter) towards a black vertical bar with white flanks, bar widths 20 to 70 deg in 10 deg steps, Michelson contrast 0.95; maximum likelihood comparisons of circular distributions
conditions: wild-collected adults from Isla Solarte, Panama; natural daylight beneath a diffuser; Michelson contrast 0.95; N = 40 to 52 animals per bar width, each animal shown each stimulus once; tests 10:00 to 15:15 h (the species is active at night)
quote: Animals oriented towards stimuli that occupied 50 deg of the arena wall and above, according to maximum likelihood comparisons (Fig. 3A; Table 1).
note: Animals presented with 20 to 40 deg bars were found to be disoriented relative to stimulus position. The Results give a 50% confidence interval for the psychometric threshold of 41 to 63 deg, (called a 50% credible interval of a Bayesian psychometric model in the Discussion), and the Discussion says a threshold at 50 deg and above could indicate either a limit of detection or of motivation. The animal lacks discrete eyes.

note: The next sentence says animals oriented to the 60 deg stimulus at Michelson contrast 0.95. Only two contrasts below 0.95 were tested, so the contrast threshold lies between 0.1 and 0.95 on this evidence.

source.title: Modelling the visual world of a velvet worm

quote: This acute zone in the frontal part of the visual field has a resolution of about 0.11 cycles/degree.
note: A calculated value, not a behavioural test. The paper says the histological preparation may introduce shrinkage and deformation artefacts and that the method is based entirely on geometrical optics and ignores wave optical phenomena. It also says its results confirm behavioural measurements from previous studies on velvet worms; the numbers of those studies were not read. Resolution is the cut-off from the full width at half maximum of each receptor's angular sensitivity in Fourier space; receptor spacing (about 2.5 µm centre to centre) does not enter as a Nyquist limit, and the lens refractive index is 1.44 in the Methods but 1.485 in the Results.
